parts.title: My first summer job
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
On my sixteenth birthday, my uncle offered me a job in his restaurant for the summer. I was thrilled, until I saw what I had to do. My first week was spent in the kitchen, washing plates and cutting onions, and by Friday my hands were red and my eyes were sore. I was so disappointed that I thought about quitting.

Then one Saturday evening, one of the waiters did not turn up. My uncle looked at me and asked, 'Do you think you can carry plates?' I said yes before I could think. It was the busiest night of the week, and I was so nervous that I dropped a spoon in front of my first customers, a family with three small children. The children laughed, and then, to my relief, the mother laughed too.

After that, I got better quickly. I learned to remember orders without writing them down, and to smile even when somebody was rude. A cook called Marta taught me to say 'hot plate, please!' when I was carrying food through the busy kitchen, so that nobody walked into me. By the end of the summer, I was earning tips, and I had saved enough money to buy a second-hand guitar.

I have not decided what I want to do when I leave school. But I know that I do not want to sit behind a desk all day. Working with people can be tiring, but it is never boring.

questions.prompt: How did the writer feel at the end of the first week?
questions.explanation: She was disappointed and thought about quitting after a week of washing plates and cutting onions.

questions.prompt: Why did she carry plates on Saturday evening?
options: She asked for a better job.
Her uncle wanted to test her.
She wanted to earn more money.
A waiter had not come to work.
questions.explanation: One of the waiters did not turn up and her uncle asked her to help.

questions.prompt: What happened when she dropped the spoon?
options: The family laughed in a friendly way.
The customers were very angry with her.
Her uncle sent her home for the evening.
The mother asked her to leave the table.
questions.explanation: The children laughed and then the mother laughed too, to her relief.

questions.prompt: What did Marta teach her?
options: To cook some very simple meals
To warn people about hot food
questions.explanation: Marta taught her to say 'hot plate, please!' so nobody walked into her.

questions.prompt: What does she say about her future?
options: She plans to study music at college.
She wants to work with people.
She will become a cook one day.
questions.explanation: She does not want to sit behind a desk all day and says working with people is never boring.

parts.title: The baker who starts at three
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
At three o'clock in the morning, when most of the town is asleep, Jorge is already at work. He is a baker, and he has the strangest timetable of anyone he knows. [1] His friends call him 'the owl', but he says that he would not change it for anything.

The first job is to prepare the dough, which has to rest for several hours. [2] Then the ovens must be heated, and the loaves are shaped by hand, one at a time. By six o'clock, the bakery smells wonderful.

The shop opens at seven, and by then a line of customers is waiting outside. Some of them have been buying bread from him for thirty years. [3] "I know exactly who likes their bread well baked and who prefers it soft," he says.

However, the job also has its problems. He sleeps in the afternoon, which means that he often misses family events. [4] In winter, the walk to work in the dark is cold and lonely.

Jorge hopes that his daughter will take over the bakery one day. [5] "She helped me last Christmas," he says proudly, "and she did not complain once, even though she had to get up at two."
sentences: He remembers most of them by name.
In the meantime, he mixes the ingredients for the cakes.
She gets up at six and takes the first bus to school.
Bread was first baked in ovens made of clay.
He finishes his work when others are just beginning theirs.
Another problem is that he has very little time to relax in the evenings.
His shop is the oldest in the town.
He is not sure that she wants to, but she has shown some interest.

gaps.explanation: "The strangest timetable" is explained by sentence A: he starts when others are asleep and finishes when they begin; the next sentence is about his nickname.
The dough must rest for hours; "In the meantime" says what he does while waiting, and then "the ovens must be heated".
Customers have bought bread for thirty years; "He remembers most of them by name" leads to what he knows about their preferences.
He misses family events; "Another problem" adds to the list, and the next sentence gives winter as a further problem.
He hopes his daughter will take over; he is not sure she wants to, but she has shown interest, and the next sentence describes how she helped.

parts.title: Writing a good CV
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: A CV is a short document that tells an employer about you. It should be clear and easy to [1], so use short sentences and a simple layout. Start with your name and contact details, and then list your education, beginning with the most [2] school or college. If you have no work experience, write about activities that show your skills, such as babysitting or helping at a club. Always check your CV carefully for spelling [3]. Many employers will not even read a CV that contains errors. [4] you have finished, ask a friend or a teacher to read it. Be honest about what you can do, because you may [5] to prove it in an interview. Finally, send your CV with a short letter explaining why you would like [6] job.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: A CV should be easy to read.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: You list education starting with the most recent school or college.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: Employers do not like spelling mistakes; the next sentence says they do not read CVs with errors.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: "When you have finished" says the time to ask a friend to read it.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: "May have to prove" means it is possible that you will need to prove it.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: "Why you would like this job" refers to the job that you are applying for.

parts.title: A job application
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Dear Mr Rossi,
I am writing [1] apply for the job of waiter at your café, which I saw advertised in the window. I am sixteen years old, and I [2] looking for a weekend job. I have [3] experience, but I am a quick learner, and I enjoy meeting people. At school, I was a member of the drama club, [4] has helped me to feel confident. I am free every Saturday and Sunday [5] the whole summer. I enclose my CV, and I look forward [6] hearing from you.
Yours sincerely,

gaps.explanation: "I am writing to apply" gives the purpose of the letter.
The present continuous "am looking" needs the verb be.
"No experience, but a quick learner" shows the contrast.
"Which" refers to the whole fact of being in the drama club.
"For the whole summer" gives the length of time.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: alcuin
turns.text: Hello, Bernadette, this is Alcuin from Greenfield Offices, calling about your interview tomorrow. We said ten o’clock, but I’m afraid the director has an important meeting, so we need to change it. First I thought of eleven, but then you wouldn’t have time to meet the team afterwards. So we have agreed on a time that is only half an hour later than before. That should be easy for you, I hope. Please come to the main reception and ask for me. Bring your passport, and call me if there is a problem. See you tomorrow. Goodbye!

question.prompt: What time is Bernadette's interview now?
question.explanation: The old time was ten and eleven was only an idea, so the interview is half an hour later than the first time.

turns.speaker: cyril
turns.text: So, Dorcas, the advert said ten pounds an hour, but that is for people over twenty-one.

turns.speaker: dorcas
turns.text: I’m nineteen, so I suppose it’s lower.

turns.speaker: cyril
turns.text: Right. For your age we pay a smaller amount. After six months it goes up to nine pounds, and if you stay a year, it’s the full rate.

turns.speaker: dorcas
turns.text: What is it at the beginning, then?

turns.speaker: cyril
turns.text: Seven pounds fifty. I know it’s not much, but there’s a free lunch and you keep the tips.

turns.speaker: dorcas
turns.text: OK, I understand. It’s my first job, so I’m happy to start there.

turns.speaker: cyril
turns.text: Great. I’ll prepare the contract for tomorrow.

question.prompt: How much will the girl earn per hour?
question.explanation: Ten pounds is the full rate for people over twenty-one and nine pounds comes after six months; at the beginning she gets seven pounds fifty.

turns.speaker: flavia
turns.text: Hello, Ezra. Welcome. I hoped you could start next Monday, but the computers aren’t ready yet.

turns.speaker: ezra
turns.text: No problem. Could I start this Friday instead? I’m free all day.

turns.speaker: flavia
turns.text: Friday is the day of the staff meeting, so everybody will be busy and no one can train you. The engineer finishes his work on Tuesday, so the best day would be the day after that.

turns.speaker: ezra
turns.text: That’s fine. What time should I come?

turns.speaker: flavia
turns.text: At nine, to the front desk. Bring your bank details and a photo for your card.

turns.speaker: ezra
turns.text: Perfect. I’ll be here.

question.prompt: When will the man start work?
question.explanation: Monday is too early because the computers are not ready and Friday is the staff meeting; the engineer finishes on Tuesday, so he starts the day after.

turns.speaker: gerard_x
turns.text: For your first day at the café, Hypatia, you’ll need to wear something smart. Last year the staff wore green shirts and long aprons, but we stopped that.

turns.speaker: hypatia
turns.text: Does the café give out uniforms, then?

turns.speaker: gerard_x
turns.text: We thought about it, but it was too expensive, so you wear your own clothes. Just keep it simple.

turns.speaker: hypatia
turns.text: What colour?

turns.speaker: gerard_x
turns.text: A clean white shirt and dark trousers, black is best.

turns.speaker: hypatia
turns.text: I have those. I’ll iron them tonight.

turns.speaker: gerard_x
turns.text: Good. And please bring flat shoes, you’ll be on your feet all day.

question.prompt: What will the woman wear to work?
options: A green shirt with an apron
A white shirt and black trousers
question.explanation: The green shirt and apron were last year and there is no uniform, so she wears her own white shirt and black trousers.

turns.speaker: isolde
turns.text: Jasper, do we have our break at twelve on Saturdays, like during the week?

turns.speaker: jasper
turns.text: No, Saturday is the busiest time, so it’s different. The manager first said half past twelve, but the delivery arrives then, so we have to stay.

turns.speaker: isolde
turns.text: So later than that?

turns.speaker: jasper
turns.text: Yes, the lorry usually leaves at a quarter to one, and then we eat at one. Also, it’s a full hour, not thirty minutes.

turns.speaker: isolde
turns.text: Brilliant! Maybe a long lunch in the park.

turns.speaker: jasper
turns.text: Just remember to be back on time.

question.prompt: When is the break on Saturdays?
question.explanation: Twelve is the weekday break and half past twelve was only the first idea, but the delivery lorry leaves at a quarter to one, so they eat at one.

turns.speaker: kendrick
turns.text: Hi Lucy, it’s Kendrick from Sunny Bakery. A message about tomorrow, your first day. Come at eight, to the back door, not the shop door. Usually Mrs Clark, the manager, shows new staff around, but she’s on holiday this week. I thought of asking one of our regular customers, an old friend who comes every morning and knows everything, but she’s busy too. So the man who started the bakery thirty years ago, Mr Pike, wants to do it himself. He’s very proud of the place, and he loves to talk to new people. Bring a pen. See you!

question.prompt: Who will meet Lucy on her first day?
question.explanation: The manager is on holiday and the regular customer is busy, so the man who started the bakery, Mr Pike, will meet her.

turns.speaker: norma
turns.text: Marius, are you going to drive to the new office? There’s a car park.

turns.speaker: marius
turns.text: I thought so, but it costs eight pounds a day.

turns.speaker: norma
turns.text: A bicycle then? It’s only five kilometres.

turns.speaker: marius
turns.text: I nearly bought one last week, but with the hills and the rain, no thanks.

turns.speaker: norma
turns.text: What about the number nine? It stops right in front of the office.

turns.speaker: marius
turns.text: That’s what I’ll do. It’s cheap, and I can read a book on the way.

turns.speaker: norma
turns.text: Sensible! And you don’t have to look for a place to park.

turns.speaker: marius
turns.text: Exactly. I’ll get a monthly ticket this weekend.

question.prompt: How will the man travel to work?
question.explanation: The car park is expensive and the hills and rain stop him from cycling; he chooses the number nine, which stops in front of the office.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: octavius
turns.text: Tomorrow’s your big day, Prudence. How are you feeling?

turns.speaker: prudence
turns.text: Terrible. I can’t eat or sleep. What if I make a mistake on the first day?

turns.speaker: octavius
turns.text: Everyone does. You were the best in the interview, and I’m sure you will do well.

turns.speaker: prudence
turns.text: I know, and my boss is really kind, so I’m not angry or upset about anything. It’s just that I’ve never worked in a hospital before. Nobody knows me there.

turns.speaker: octavius
turns.text: You’ll be fine. I felt the same on my first day, and now I love it.

turns.speaker: prudence
turns.text: Maybe. Can you call me tonight?

turns.speaker: octavius
turns.text: Of course.

question.explanation: Octavius is sure she will do well and she likes her boss, but she is nervous because she has never worked in a hospital.

turns.speaker: rosamunde
turns.text: Quillan, can I have a word before you go? I know you have a dentist appointment at four.

turns.speaker: quillan
turns.text: Yes, I do. Do you want me to cancel it? I can, if it’s important.

turns.speaker: rosamunde
turns.text: No, no, don’t do that. You’ve changed it twice already. I was going to ask you to work on Saturday, but then I remembered your sister’s wedding.

turns.speaker: quillan

turns.speaker: rosamunde
turns.text: I just need your sales reports. If you finish them before four, you can leave. Otherwise Mr Tan will be angry tomorrow.

turns.speaker: quillan
turns.text: It will take an hour. I’ll start now.

question.prompt: What does the manager want the man to do?
question.explanation: She does not want him to cancel the dentist or to work on Saturday; she needs the sales reports finished before four.

turns.speaker: severus
turns.text: You look happy, Thomasine. What’s your news?

turns.speaker: thomasine
turns.text: I’ve been offered a job at the radio station! I had the interview on Monday, and they phoned this morning.

turns.speaker: severus
turns.text: Congratulations! Is the pay good?

turns.speaker: thomasine
turns.text: It’s not high, to be honest, but it’s more than I expected for a first job. And the place is only ten minutes from home, so no long journey.

turns.speaker: severus
turns.text: So what’s the problem?

turns.speaker: thomasine
turns.text: There’s no problem! I’m just so surprised, I can’t believe it. It’s exactly what I wanted since I was twelve.

question.prompt: How does the girl feel about her news?
options: She is very pleased with the offer.
She thinks the pay is too low.
She worries that it is too far.
question.explanation: The pay is not high and the place is near, so neither is a problem; she is delighted because it is the job she always wanted.

turns.speaker: ulysse
turns.text: Does your brother still work at the bank, Valentine?

turns.speaker: valentine
turns.text: Yes, and he hates it. He says it’s boring and the hours are long.

turns.speaker: ulysse
turns.text: Then why doesn’t he leave? Does he get on well with his colleagues there?

turns.speaker: valentine
turns.text: Not really, they’re all very serious. And it’s not that he has nothing else. He’s had two offers this year.

turns.speaker: ulysse
turns.text: So what is it?

turns.speaker: valentine
turns.text: The money. He earns so much that every other job would be a step down. He wants to buy a house.

turns.speaker: ulysse
turns.text: I understand. It’s difficult to give that up.

question.prompt: Why does the girl's brother stay in his job?
question.explanation: He does not like the people and he has had other offers, but he earns so much that any other job would be a step down.

turns.speaker: wilfred
turns.text: How’s the new job at the garden centre, Xaviera?

turns.speaker: xaviera
turns.text: Great. I thought I’d miss working in an office, but no. I’m outside most days, in the fresh air, even when it’s cold.

turns.speaker: wilfred
turns.text: And you carry all those plants?

turns.speaker: xaviera
turns.text: Ha! Yes, my arms are strong now, but I don’t love it. And the customers can be rude when they’re in a hurry. Some are lovely, but others complain about everything.

turns.speaker: wilfred
turns.text: So what’s the best bit?

turns.speaker: xaviera
turns.text: Honestly, the sun on my face at eleven in the morning, with a cup of tea. I would never go back to an office.

question.prompt: What does the girl like about her job?
question.explanation: She does not love lifting and some customers are rude; she enjoys being in the fresh air and the sun, and she would never go back to an office.

turns.speaker: zeno
turns.text: Is your father still at the farm, Yseult?

turns.speaker: yseult_x
turns.text: Yes, thirty years now! It’s funny. He only went there for one summer, to earn some money before university, but he liked it so much that he never left.

turns.speaker: zeno
turns.text: I thought he went to university.

turns.speaker: yseult_x
turns.text: He did think about it, but he didn’t go in the end. My uncle changes jobs every year, but my dad is the opposite. He says he found the right place right away.

turns.speaker: zeno
turns.text: That’s lucky.

turns.speaker: yseult_x
turns.text: I think so too. I’d like that.

question.prompt: What does the girl say about her father's career?
options: He took a summer job and stayed.
He studied for many years first.
question.explanation: It was only for one summer to earn money, but he liked it and never left; it is her uncle who changes jobs, not her dad.

parts.title: A manager welcomes new staff
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Hillcrest Garden Centre. I’m Aurelia, the manager. Before you begin your first day, I want to explain a few things. First, the hours. The shop opens to customers at nine, and you will see in your contract that work starts at eight, but we changed that last week, so it’s half past eight, which gives you time for a cup of tea first. I know it’s early for some of you. The lunch break is at one o’clock. The old break was an hour long, but now we have thirty minutes, so you will finish earlier in the afternoon. On clothes: everyone wears a green uniform, which I will give to you in a moment. You can’t wear your own shirt. You must also wear a name badge, so that customers know who you are. Please keep it on the left side. Now, where to work. We have three sections: the plant section, the tools and the café. Sam is already working in the plant section, near the greenhouses. He’ll show you what to do, and he’s very friendly. The tools section is Maria’s, and if you want to work in the café, you should ask me. Now some safety. When you lift heavy bags of soil or compost you must wear gloves, and also good shoes, not sandals. Please bend your knees, and don’t lift alone if it’s too heavy. And finally, what to do if the alarm rings. The main door at the front is for customers, but you should not use it. The fire exit is at the back of the shop, behind the tool section, and it’s marked with a green sign. Meet outside by the big tree. Does everyone understand? Great. Let’s start.

gaps.prompt: The working day now begins at ___
gaps.explanation: The contract says eight, but it was changed last week to half past eight.

gaps.prompt: Employees get a lunch break of ___ minutes
gaps.explanation: The old break was an hour, but now they have thirty minutes.

gaps.prompt: Besides a green uniform, staff must wear a name ___
gaps.explanation: They cannot wear their own shirt; they wear the uniform and a name badge on the left side.

gaps.prompt: A colleague called Sam works in the ___ section
gaps.explanation: Tools is Maria’s section and the café is for people who ask the manager; Sam is in the plant section.

gaps.prompt: Heavy bags of soil must be lifted wearing ___
gaps.explanation: They also need good shoes, but the equipment for the bags is gloves.

gaps.prompt: In an emergency the exit to use is at the ___ of the shop
gaps.explanation: The front door is for customers; the fire exit is at the back.

parts.title: An interview with a paramedic
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Wolfgang, you’ve been a paramedic for fifteen years. Why did you choose this job?

turns.speaker: wolfgang
turns.text: It wasn’t because of my parents, they both worked in banks, and honestly, I never thought about hospitals. And I’m not one of those people who just wants to drive fast, although it’s fun. When I was twelve, my grandfather fell in the garden. A paramedic came, and she was so kind and so calm that I never forgot her. I decided I wanted to be like her.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What are the shifts like?

turns.speaker: wolfgang
turns.text: They are definitely not quiet. The night can be very busy. I don’t think they’re short, though; we normally work twelve hours, from seven to seven. The first hours pass quickly, then you start to feel tired. You need good food and a good sleep afterwards.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What quality does a paramedic need most?

turns.speaker: wolfgang
turns.text: Many people say being fast, and I do drive quickly sometimes, but it’s not the most important thing. Strong arms help when you carry people, of course. But I believe the main thing is to stay calm, because when you are calm, the patient feels safe, and you think clearly. A panicking paramedic is no use to anyone.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How do you deal with the stress?

turns.speaker: wolfgang
turns.text: Some people write a diary about their day, and I tried it, but it didn’t work for me. Holidays help, but you can’t take long ones very often. What really helps is talking with the others in the team. After a difficult day we sit in the station with our colleagues and just chat, and everybody understands.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What made you happiest last year?

turns.speaker: wolfgang
turns.text: The hospital gave us a small prize, a certificate, and it was nice, but I forgot about it quickly. My grandfather came to the station once, years ago, but not last year. No, it was a card from a family. We helped their little girl after an accident in June, and in December they sent us a card with her drawing. I put it on the wall of the station.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What advice would you give to young people who would like your job?

turns.speaker: wolfgang
turns.text: Learn first aid now, there are courses everywhere, and be a volunteer, with the Red Cross for example. You don’t need to study at a famous university first, and you certainly don’t have to work in a hospital kitchen! Just show that you care about people.

options: His parents worked in a hospital.
He admired one who helped his grandfather.
He wanted to drive very fast.
questions.explanation: His parents worked in banks and driving fast is not the reason; a calm paramedic helped his grandfather when he was twelve.

questions.prompt: What does he say about his shifts?
options: They are always quiet and calm.
They are short but quite difficult.
questions.explanation: They are not quiet and not short; they work from seven to seven.

questions.prompt: What does he think is the most important quality?
questions.explanation: Speed does not matter most and strong arms only help; the main thing is to stay calm.

questions.prompt: How do paramedics deal with stress?
questions.explanation: The diary did not work for him and long holidays are rare; what helps is talking with the team.

questions.prompt: What made him particularly happy last year?
questions.explanation: He forgot the prize quickly and his grandfather did not come last year; the family’s card with a drawing made him happy.

questions.prompt: What advice does he give to young people?

Work in a large hospital kitchen
